definition: In machine learning, a linear classifier makes a classification decision for each object based on a linear combination of its features.
details: A simpler definition is to say that a linear classifier is one whose decision boundaries are linear. Such classifiers work well for practical problems such as document classification, and more generally for problems with many variables (features), reaching accuracy levels comparable to non-linear classifiers while taking less time to train and use.

explainer.lead: A linear classifier decides an object's class from a linear combination of its features, giving linear decision boundaries. It matters because on problems with many features, such as document classification, it can approach non-linear classifier accuracy while training and running faster.

tiers.eli5: You score each item by adding up its features with fixed weights and pick the class with the higher score; sorting is done with a straight line or flat surface.
tiers.practitioner: Often chosen for high-dimensional problems like document classification because it is cheap to train and use; a pitfall is that it cannot capture boundaries that are not linear.
tiers.paperLevel: Class decisions are based on a linear combination of features, so decision boundaries are linear; performance comparable to non-linear classifiers is reported particularly for problems with many variables.

explainer.example: Classifying documents by summing weighted counts of their features; with many features, accuracy comparable to non-linear classifiers is reached with less training and use time.
